 Judgment

The present appeal is filed by the appellant/claimant challenging the judgment and award dated 11.09.2014 in MVC.No.694/2013 passed by the Court of the Addl. Judge, Small Causes and Senior Civil Judge, MACT, Mysore, for seeking enhancement of compensation.

entities.text: Addl. Judge, Small Causes and Senior Civil Judge, MACT, Mysore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Brief facts of the case are that, on 17.06.2013 at 1.00 pm., the claimant being a pillion rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-09-EW-4136 was going towards Infosys Road, near Jaimathaji Daba Junction, at that time, 1st respondent being a driver of the car bearing Reg.No.KA-09-N-5904 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motor cycle of the claimant.

Due to which,
the claimant fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

3. Heard the arguments from both sides and perused the records.
4.
The Tribunal has awarded compensation under various heads as follows:

1 Loss of studies Rs.10,000/-
2 Pain and sufferings Rs.20,000/- 3 Medicines & treatment Rs.1,72,917/- 4 Conveyance & special diet Rs.10,000/- 4 Attendant charges Rs.12,000/- 5 Loss of amenities of life Rs.10,000/-
5. In the present case, the medical evidence proves that the claimant had sustained fracture of shaft of right femur and abrasion all over the body, which is the grievous injury.
The femur bone is the major bone, which is the weight bearing capacity bone.
If femur bone is fractured, then it affects substantially.
Therefore, the compensation of Rs.20,000/- awarded under the head pain and suffering is on the lesser side and the same is enhanced to Rs.40,000/-.
6. The claimant has produced the medical bill and hospitalization charges worth Rs.2,06,727/- as per Ex.P.10.

The Tribunal has deducted a sum of Rs.33,810/-
and granted compensation of Rs.1,72,917/-.
The said medical bills of Rs.33,810/- are issued by the hospitals at Coimbatore.

The Tribunal has observed that there is no evidence to show that the claimant was advised to take rest in the said hostel or she travelled by any vehicle from the said hostel to her college and she took treatment in the above said hospitals.
The reasons assigned for reduction is not correct.
The medical bills issued are not found to be double claim or duplication.

Just because, the records are not produced for taking treatment in the hospital, it does not mean that the claimant has not made expenditure and for the injuries sustained, the claimant might have taken treatment and follow-up treatment and on some occasions, she could have been admitted as an inpatient.
Therefore, the medical bills produced are not found to be double claim or duplication.
Therefore, the reduction made by the Tribunal is not correct.
Therefore, the claimant is entitled for compensation to the extent of medical bills produced by the claimant.
Accordingly, a sum of Rs.2,07,000/- is awarded under the head medical expenses and hospitalization charges.
7. The Tribunal has not awarded compensation under the head loss of future income due to disability.
The doctor had stated that the claimant has suffered permanent physical disability at 18.83% in relation to right leg.

The Tribunal had taken the disability at 6% by taking 1/3rd of it and even the Tribunal opined that the said disability at 6% is negligible one and not awarded compensation under the head loss of future income.
The said observation made by the Tribunal is not correct.
The claimant had suffered fracture of shaft of right femur and abrasion all over the body.
The femur bone is the weight bearing bone.
The loss of earning capacity due to disability cannot be considered strictly in a mathematical formula way.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar and Another 1 was pleased to laid down the principle of law as to how to assess the functional disability affecting the earning capacity/future income.

sentences.text: Then such fracture to the femur bone affects to some extent the working capacity of the claimant.
For this, some percentage is to be adopted as functional disability.
Considering the nature of injuries sustained and the evidence of the doctor, functional disability at 10% is to be considered.
8. The claimant is a student studying in II year of Bachelor of Technology and she was aged 21 years as on the date of the accident.
Therefore, considering the engineering course, which was pursuing by the claimant, it is just and proper to take notional income at Rs.10,000/- p.m.
As the claimant was aged 21 years as on the date of the accident, the appropriate multiplier applicable is 18.

Hence, the compensation under the head loss of future income due to disability is re-assessed and quantified as follows:
Rs.10,000/- x 10% x 18 x 12=Rs.2,16,000/-
Accordingly, compensation of Rs.2,16,000/- is awarded under the head loss of future income due to disability.
9. The compensation of Rs.10,000/- awarded under the head loss of amenities is on the lesser side and the same is enhanced to Rs.40,000/- under the said head.

10. The compensation of Rs.10,000/- is awarded under the head conveyance & special diet and Rs.12,000/- is awarded under the head attendant charges, which are on the lesser side and the same is enhanced to Rs.30,000/- under the heads conveyance & special diet and attendant charges.

11. The compensation awarded under the head loss of studies is already included under the head loss of future income due to disability and the same is modified as it is included under the head loss of future income due to disability.
12. The compensation of Rs.20,000/- is awarded under the head future medical expenses.
13. The claimant is a woman aged 21 years and has suffered fracture of femur bone of right leg and even though, the fracture is stated to have been reunited, but to some extent, limp is there.
Therefore, the said limping affects the marriage prospects of the claimant to some extent.
Accordingly, compensation of Rs.25,000/- is awarded under the head loss of marriage prospects.

. Thus, in all, the appellant/claimant is entitled to the compensation as follows:
1 Pain and sufferings Rs.40,000/- 2 Medicines & treatment Rs.2,07,000/- 3 Loss of future earning Rs.2,16,000/-
capacity due to disability 4 Conveyance & special diet Rs.30,000/-

15.
The Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.2,34,917/-, but the appellant/claimant is entitled to total compensation of Rs.5,78,000/-.
Hence, the appellant/claimant is entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.3,43,083/- (Rs.5,78,000/- - Rs.2,34,917/-).

Therefore, the appellant/claimant is entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.3,43,083/- along with interest at the - 11 - rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization, in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.

16. Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i. Appeal is allowed-in-part.
ii.

The impugned judgment and award dated 11.09.2014 in MVC.No.694/2013 passed by the Court of the Addl. Judge, Small Causes and Senior Civil Judge, MACT, Mysore,
is modified to the extent that the appellant/claimant is entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.3,43,083/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization, in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.
